# Read-back

Two T75 flasks of adherent HEK293 cells at 90% confluence are being passaged and split 1:6 into four new T75 flasks (two from each original flask) to expand the culture. The work is performed by one operator over approximately 2–3 hours, with no hard deadline stated, so the goal is to finish as early as the protocol allows. The operator must sequence work around single-instance shared equipment: one biosafety cabinet (which can hold only one open flask at a time, creating a queue), one 37 °C water bath (pre-warming media), one CO₂ incubator (holding flasks during trypsinization and settling), one benchtop centrifuge (spinning suspensions), and one microscope with haemocytometer (checking confluence and counting cells). The protocol is split into three phases: prep (wiping cabinet, checking both source flasks), parallel processing of flask A (aspirate, trypsinize, neutralize, spin, count, seed two new flasks) and flask B (same steps, but sequenced to avoid cabinet bottlenecks—flask B starts its cabinet work the moment flask A exits, and flask B's neutralization waits until flask A has already done its cabinet work again), and finishing (cabinet cleanup and logging). The text is complete with no truncations or missing sections.
